title: Thermodynamics
confusion: ❌ 'In an isothermal process no heat is exchanged.' ✅ In isothermal, ΔU = 0 so Q = W. All heat becomes work. Adiabatic has Q = 0.
❌ 'In an adiabatic process temperature is constant.' ✅ In adiabatic, Q = 0 so ΔU = −W. Temperature changes when work is done.
❌ 'First law forbids all perpetual motion machines.' ✅ First law only forbids PMM1 (energy creation). Second law forbids PMM2 (100% heat-to-work conversion).
❌ 'Entropy can decrease, so second law is wrong.' ✅ Local entropy can decrease, but universal entropy always increases in spontaneous processes.
notes: **First law of thermodynamics:** ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW — heat supplied to a gas partly increases internal energy and partly does external work.
**Work in isothermal expansion:** W = nRT ln(V₂/V₁). In an isothermal process (constant T), ΔU = 0. In an adiabatic process (no heat exchange), ΔQ = 0.
**Second law / entropy:** entropy of the universe always increases in a spontaneous process; ΔS = ΔQ/T.
**Carnot engine:** efficiency η = 1 − T₂/T₁. Ideal efficiency depends only on the temperatures of source and sink.
